checks: For necessity of the transversal criterion, restrict an independent choice to the test set. In the tight-subset induction case its independent choices span the whole tight span, and the dimension inequality on the union of that subset and any complementary subset gives the criterion in the quotient. Any choice of preimages of the resulting independent quotient representatives joins the tight basis independently.

In the no-tight-subset case a nonzero last representative exists by the singleton dimension bound. Each nonempty subset of the remaining indices is proper in the original family and has at least one dimension to lose; passage to the line quotient preserves all dimension inequalities. The one-set base case is immediate; the empty family, when needed, has the empty independent choice.

Universal zero-convex-hull inclusion means every transversal has a nontrivial linear dependence, so there is positive deficiency. If A has maximum deficiency, comparing A with A∪B for B disjoint gives dim(W_A+W_B)−dim W_A≥|B|. A nonempty proper maximizer would admit fixed independent outside representatives in the quotient. For each inside choice, projecting its full convex dependence forces all outside coefficients to zero while inside coefficients still sum to one. This contradicts inclusion minimality. No closure, compactness or strictly positive coefficients are needed; the singleton case is exactly the zero menu.

The common annihilator has codimension equal to the span rank, by using a basis of the finite covector span in the joint evaluation map. The statement is abstract and does not assert that any geometric circuit menus satisfy the hypothesis.
